text:
Sam: Hey team — Aperture Financial is evaluating a migration off NimbusAI to Redwood. They want a POC that proves prompt parity and minimal UX delta. They also flagged pricing questions for heavy streaming workloads and a security/INFRA questionnaire. Can we get a short plan and known incompatibilities they should expect?
Anya: Thanks Sam. Quick Qs: what are Aperture's main success metrics for the POC (latency, token cost, exact-match accuracy, hallucination rate)? Do they have a sample corpus or prompt bundle?
Sam: Aperture cares about 1) 99th perc latency <= 200ms for chat paths, 2) token costs <= current spend or show ~30% savings, and 3) <2% prompt-output parity diffs on our eval set. They can share a 2000 prompt sample.
Omar: Good to know. High-level incompatibilities we've seen when swapping from NimbusAI -> Redwood: tokenization differences (rarely changes token counts by 1-4%), default stop-token behavior, streaming chunk framing (Nimbus streams per-sentence), and default decoding seeds/temperature. Also Nimbus had a proprietary post-processing step for trailing whitespace.
Omar: Quick mapping we recommend (will include in POC adapter):
```json
{
  "temperature": 0.0,
  "top_p": 0.95,
  "stop": ["<END>", "\n\n"],
  "max_new_tokens": 256,
  "streaming_chunk_size": 64
}
```
Anya: For prompt parity: make all stop tokens explicit in the prompt and append a deterministic suffix if you relied on Nimbus implicit trimming. Example change we made for a fintech prompt: 
```diff
- "Summarize customer's last 3 transactions."
+ "Summarize customer's last 3 transactions. <END>"
```
Sam: Pricing question: Aperture's finance team asks if streaming tokens are billed same as non-streaming and whether we offer committed discounts for high-throughput slots.
Anya: Streaming billing = token-based (same unit cost) + small per-connection overhead on Dedicated. For Dedicated we can propose a committed throughput contract (monthly GPU pool) with tiered discounts. I'll pull sample numbers for a 3M token/month baseline.
Linda: Security notes from compliance — Aperture requires SOC2 + customer-managed KMS in any Private deployment, plus support for IP allowlists and audit log export to their SIEM. They also expect us to answer an encryption-in-transit and at-rest Q.
Anya: We can do Private (VPC) with KMS/HSM + audit logs shipped to their S3/LogDest. For Hosted, we can offer a DPA + SOC2 report and an NDA, but KMS only on Dedicated/Private.
Omar: Engineering POC checklist (short):
- ingest 2k prompts into eval harness
- run baseline on Nimbus (provided by Aperture) and Redwood dev cluster
- apply adapter mapping (tokenizer, stop tokens, decoding config)
- diff outputs, flag tokens/formatting mismatches
- iterate prompt changes (add explicit stops, canonicalize whitespace)
We should automate diffs and surface a small set of 'template rewrites' to give Aperture engineers.
Sam: Timeline ask from Aperture: 2-week technical POC + 1 week of analysis. Realistic?
Omar: Yes, 2 weeks is feasible if we get their sample bundle and access to their baseline inference logs within 48 hours. We need a small Dedicated dev slot for stable latency measurements — else noisy multi-tenant hosted metrics won't be comparable.
Anya: I'll draft a short SOW and a presales pricing sketch. Proposed next steps for this thread: 
- Sam: collect 2k prompt bundle + baseline Nimbus outputs (ideally with request ids).
- Anya: send SOW + pricing sketch and NDA template by EOD tomorrow.
- Omar: provision a 1-week Dedicated dev slot and run the initial parity job once bundle is in.
- Linda: prepare security Q answers (KMS, SOC2, network controls).
Sam: I'll ping Aperture infra and legal to get the bundle and sign the NDA. Also they want an architecture note explaining fallback: can we fall back to a Nimbus-compatible variant if we see regression?
Omar: We can implement runtime routing: primary->Redwood, fallback->Nimbus shim (or a conservative Redwood config) for L0 requests. We'll include a simple feature-flagged fallback policy in the POC.
infra-bot: capacity-check: Dedicated dev slot (small) available Tue-Wed next week, auto-reserved for 48h on request.
Anya: Great — I'll schedule the kickoff and put a short runbook on the shared drive. Anyone want to add items to the POC runbook?
Sam: Please include a quick table with expected token delta tolerances (e.g., +/- 5% tokens, <=2% output diffs). Aperture will use that for acceptance.
Omar: Adding that. Also recommend we capture a handful of regression prompts with golden answers to track hallucination delta.
Linda: I'll add the security checklist and required artifacts (SOC2 report link, KMS diagram, entitlements matrix).
Sam: Thanks all — will update after I hear back from Aperture infra. :thumbsup:
